answer: A farm must thus place its own capital behind every alias it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. Because the copper liability is entered in the oasis ledger at admission, the beacon audit reveals the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A sponsor carries 39% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. That is 14 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
